clue.text: Go to grab bird that's little

indicators.note: one piece grabbing another holds it inside, so the bird sits within the word for go

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, to pee
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: An instruction to seize a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite is a synonym for small or dainty, especially of a woman's build.

clue.text: So haddock the chippie's future then? English homes all have one

parts.words: So haddock the chippie's future then?
parts.note: if a fish-and-chip shop moves on from cod to haddock, its future is life after cod

explanation.surface: A fish-shop joke about haddock replacing cod.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippie is a British fish-and-chip shop, where cod is the classic fish; with cod scarce, haddock may be its post-cod future.
explanation.definitionFit: Every address in England has a postcode, the letter-and-number code for mail delivery.

clue.text: Sweet to consider as salt

parts.note: a tart is a sweet pastry dessert
to rate is to consider or regard

explanation.surface: A dessert regarded as being salty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a salt of tartaric acid, as in chemistry.

clue.text: Play about king having nothing as capital

indicators.note: the play word goes round the king's letter

parts.note: to toy is to play
K is the chess abbreviation for king
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A drama about a king who has nothing becomes a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Alien killer zapping ghoul in the end

indicators.note: to zap something is to destroy it, so a letter is wiped out of the killer

parts.note: a strangler is a murderer who throttles victims

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the word ghoul

explanation.surface: A monster-slaying alien finally destroys a ghoul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zapping' removes L, the last letter of 'ghoul' (flagged by 'in the end'), from STRANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is an outsider or foreigner, which is one sense of alien.

clue.text: Given little time to get a great deal, participant rarely starts to appear attractive — in …

indicators.note: the time letter is given to the next piece, placed in front of it

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for time
a heap is a large amount

indicators.note: takes the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to entice is to make something seem attractive, to lure

explanation.surface: A contestant chasing a big deal tries to look appealing on a business show.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 6-down: the definition is 'in … the firing line from him', where 'him' is the answer to 6-down, host of this TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apprentice is the British TV business contest whose candidates are fired one by one by its host.

clue.text: … the firing line from him? Setter claiming leaderless strategy has us wound up!

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it in, so the setter holds the next pieces

parts.note: agar is a jelly that sets dishes, a setting agent

indicators.note: drops the first letter of the strategy word

parts.note: a plan is a strategy

indicators.note: turning a word up in a down clue reads it backwards

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter seizes a headless plan and we're riled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the crossword compiler but means a jelly-setting agent. 'leaderless', 'wound up' and 'claiming' each name their own step; the dash links this clue to 5-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Sugar hosts the British TV show The Apprentice and sends candidates off with his famous line, You're fired.

clue.text: Fatty piece of cake found under girl, oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first
takes the odd-numbered letters of the word girl

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy

explanation.surface: A fatty slice of cake turns up beneath a girl, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy food is oily, so fatty in texture and taste.

clue.text: Nation's sprinter, say

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like the sprinter word when spoken

parts.note: a rusher is someone who hurries, like a sprinter

explanation.surface: A country's fastest runner, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The likeness depends on a British accent, which drops the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a country, a nation spanning Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Hideous creature filmed, one out of Scream

indicators.note: says the letter for one is taken out of the scream word

parts.note: a shriek is a piercing scream
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A horror-film monster leaves the movie Scream.
explanation.walkthrough: Scream is also a horror film, which makes the surface read as cinema talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek is the ugly green ogre of the animated films, a hideous creature on screen.

clue.text: Those hi-i-i-tting birds

parts.note: the stretched-out hitting suggests beaters with extra vowels: a word for hitters with the E repeated, which names a family of birds

explanation.surface: Birds stammering as they strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaters are those hitting; spelling it with three Es, as the stretched 'hi-i-i-tting' does, gives the bird name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bee-eaters are brightly coloured birds that catch bees and other insects in flight.

clue.text: Min?

parts.note: a mine with its last letter knocked off: a pit without its base

explanation.surface: A bare abbreviation for minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Min' as MINE with its bottom letter gone: a pit (mine) that is bottomless.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit is something endless, here literally a mine with no bottom letter.

clue.text: Redhead swimmer nets redhead German boy

indicators.note: netting something catches it inside, so the fish holds the other pieces

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
the head of the word red is its first letter
Otto is a typical German boy's name

explanation.surface: A ginger angler's fish catches a ginger German lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'redhead' is read as 'red's head', the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrot-top is an informal nickname for someone with red or ginger hair.

clue.text: Dish gobbled by Dionysus, hiccuping

indicators.note: the dish is swallowed up inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: The wine god, hiccuping, wolfs down a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: The bottle bottle?

parts.note: bottle means courage, and also a bottle of drink, so this is courage that comes out of a bottle

explanation.surface: A puzzling phrase repeating the word bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means nerve or courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch courage is boldness gained from drinking alcohol.

clue.text: Revolutionary had learnt to find the centre ground

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns everything round, so the letters are overturned

explanation.surface: A radical has learnt to locate political middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The heartland is the central or core region of a country or movement.

clue.text: See 18
Old queen there to be rung before tea, finally

parts.note: something that is there to be rung is a bell, read as 'is a bell'

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word tea

explanation.surface: A former queen rings a bell to call for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Isabella was a queen of Castile, among others.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella I of Castile was a famous queen of Spain in the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Bird back after season abroad, man's problem afoot?

indicators.note: puts the bird and the season in order, bird following season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, a season as named abroad

indicators.note: the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: a crane is a long-legged wading bird
man's read as 'he is' gives the contraction he's

explanation.surface: A bird returns after a season overseas; a man's foot complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' says FALL is the US word for autumn; 'back' turns CRANE to ENARC; 'man's' is HE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen arches, or flat feet, are a condition of the foot, so a problem located on the foot.

clue.text: Fresh velvety cut or laminated edges for the buggers?

parts.note: new means fresh
velvety means soft to the touch
to hew is to cut, as with an axe
taken as written

indicators.note: takes the outer letters, first and last, of the word laminated

explanation.surface: A recipe for a soft velvety cut with laminated edges.
explanation.walkthrough: This tabloid was closed in 2011 after its staff hacked phones, so they were buggers in the eavesdropping sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists at the News of the World hacked into phones, so the paper was home to buggers in the eavesdropping sense.

clue.text: Cuckoo due to circle island without a sense of familiarity

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes round the shortened island
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of due go haywire
the island name is shown without one of its letters

parts.note: Java is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: A crazy bird due to fly round an island, without familiar feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'Cuckoo' is a bird but signals the jumble; 'without a' reads 'a' as a letter to drop, and 'to circle' sets the jumble round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Deja vu is the uncanny feeling of having already experienced the present moment.

clue.text: Turn out to see Navratilova's old rival?

definitions.meaning: Chris ... was the tennis player Martina Navratilova's great rival

explanation.definitionFit: Evert is a verb for turning outwards, and Chris Evert was a leading tennis star of the 1970s and 80s.

clue.text: Butcherbird weeps for flycatcher

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the following letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A shrike, the butcherbird, weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcherbird' looks like one word, a shrike, but 'Butcher' is the anagram signal working on BIRD WEEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web catches flies, so it is a flycatcher in a playful sense.

clue.text: So it's been repealed? That's perfect

definitions.meaning: a law that has been repealed is a former act

explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely right, and split as ex-act it describes a repealed law.

clue.text: Important to bandage knock for fruit that's purple

indicators.note: a bandage wraps round a wound, so the important word wraps round the knock

parts.note: a staple is a main or important item
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: Bandaging a bruise matters for fruit that's turned purple.
explanation.definitionFit: The star apple is a tropical fruit with purple skin, named for the star pattern inside.

clue.text: One of twelve pence in currency, reversed

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read backwards
puts the coin's letter inside the currency

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy

explanation.surface: One of twelve pennies held in a foreign currency, turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside LIRA to make LIRPA, and 'reversed' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the twelve months of the year.

clue.text: Might one catch this one song, missing the middle's flowing quality

parts.note: influenza is something one might catch
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: says the central letter of the song word is dropped

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Could one catch a song with its middle cut out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the middle' removes the central T from DITTY to leave DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluidity is the quality of flowing freely, like a liquid.

clue.text: Sporting arenas support all temporary staff, initially, in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the assembled letters run backwards

parts.note: aid is help or support

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Sports grounds back the temporary workers as they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: AID plus ATS (initials of 'all temporary staff') makes AIDATS, which 'in retirement' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, a sports arena.
